blocks.text: Sulfuric acid is soluble in water and hygroscopic, readily absorbing water vapour from the air. Anhydrous H2SO4 is a very polar liquid. It is highly corrosive to many materials and causes chemical burns on contact with the skin; it can badly burn cloth, plastic, rubber and injure the skin and eyes, so it must be handled with great care.

blocks.prompt: Why must concentrated sulfuric acid be diluted by adding acid to water and never water to acid?
blocks.explanation: Its dilution is strongly exothermic. Adding a little water to the dense acid makes the water boil at the surface and spatter acid; adding acid slowly to a large volume of water, with stirring, spreads the heat through the water safely.

items: H2SO4: colourless, viscous, odourless, hygroscopic, very polar when anhydrous; m.p. 10, b.p. 290 degrees C; specific gravity 1.83; highly corrosive.
